title: A counterexample to Naimark's problem
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's construction (2026) in ZFC of a unital, infinite-dimensional, simple C*-algebra with a faithful tracial state whose nonzero irreducible representations are all unitarily equivalent, a negative answer to Naimark's problem without additional set-theoretic axioms. The first lesson develops pure states, unique extensions, peaking sequences of projections, the excision theorem of Akemann, Anderson and Pedersen with a complete proof, cross-excision for inequivalent states and the vanishing of traces on supports of pure states. The second constructs the trace-preserving conditional expectation onto the abelian algebra generated by a peaking sequence, proves that unique state extensions with a faithful expectation preserve simplicity, that a faithful trace determines norms through moments, and that simplicity and faithful traces pass to limits. The third builds reduced amalgamated free products of tracial algebras on Hilbert modules, with the free trace and the expectation onto a factor. The fourth constructs reduced HNN adjunctions as corners of such free products, and proves uniqueness, restriction, interchange of two adjunctions and passage to limits. The fifth proves the bridge: an adjunction over two peaking sequences with matching traces joins exactly the two designated classes of pure states while every pure state keeps a unique extension. The sixth iterates the bridge transfinitely and proves that a subiteration closed under dependencies keeps unique extensions, so that every pure state is determined on a separable subalgebra. The seventh schedules the steps along the successor cardinal of the continuum and completes the construction, using the homogeneity theorem of Kishimoto, Ozawa and Sakai.
prerequisites: course foundations-of-von-neumann-algebras, lessons Representations and positive functionals: the GNS construction and the Gelfand-Naimark theorem (Proposition 3.2, Lemma 3.3, Theorems 5.4 and 5.5, Proposition 7.1a, Corollary 2.3, Theorem 8.3, Proposition 8.4), The universal enveloping von Neumann algebra of a C*-algebra and W*-algebras (Theorem 3.3, Lemma 2.1(2), Lemma 7.2, Proposition 7.3, Theorem 8.5, Lemma 11.1), Kaplansky's density theorem and its consequences (Theorem 1.3, Corollary 1.4, Theorem 11.1), C*-algebras: continuous functional calculus, automatic continuity, positive cones (Theorems 1.3 and 5.3, Corollary 4.6, Proposition 8.5), Completely positive maps (Proposition 3.2(1), Theorem 5.1(1)), Hahn-Banach, Baire and the basic theorems on Banach spaces (Theorems 8.4 and 8.5), Numerical ranges, positive matrices and co-Souslin sets (Theorem 0.1)

course hilbert-c-star-modules-and-morita-equivalence, lessons Hilbert C*-modules (Theorem 2.3), Adjointable operators (Theorem 2.2), Tensor products and C*-correspondences (Theorems 1.2, 2.1, 3.1 and Proposition 3.2)
the named hypothesis (KOS), the homogeneity theorem of Kishimoto, Ozawa and Sakai, stated in the seventh lesson and used without proof

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A counterexample to Naimark's problem in ZFC' (OpenAI, 24 Sep 2026; main.tex 49 lines, introduction 136, states 307, hnn 376, bridge 357, iteration 337, construction 139, references.bib) was read in full on 15 Oct 2026, and every step of its argument was derived again while the lessons were written: unique lifts and unitary conjugation by transitivity; peaking under restriction; decreasing excision with the support of the ideal N and the scalar corner; projection excision; cross-excision; trace-null supports; uniqueness of trace-preserving expectations; the expectation onto a peaking algebra; simplicity from (U) and a faithful expectation; the reduced amalgamated free product on Hilbert modules with its trace, faithfulness and expectation onto a factor; the HNN corner, the table of coefficients, uniqueness through moments, restriction, reordering and limits; the bridge with the endpoint criterion, Dini's theorem, matched endpoints and transfers, unique extensions, the exclusion of other joins and the return to the corner; continuous chains; the base algebra; inherited iterations; closed subiterations with the omitted pair and the commutation of adjunctions; countable determination; the count of pure states; the schedule on c+ x c+ and the construction. No error found. Differences of presentation, none a correction: the excision step uses the quotient-norm identity of the GNS space (Proposition 7.3 of the enveloping lesson) to obtain a contraction, in place of the open mapping theorem; the free product module, the identification K = L_i (x) K^(i) and the expectation onto a factor are built from the programme's Hilbert-module lessons, and the module bound and the core relation used in the bridge are stated there; purity and inequivalence of the matrix states are proved through the matrix representations; Dini's theorem for nets is proved; the moment formula for norms is proved and turned into a uniqueness criterion; the successor cardinal of the continuum is constructed and its properties derived from the programme's cardinal arithmetic; the closed-subiteration step is stated as the vanishing of the trace on reduced words. Free sources read on 15 Oct 2026: Akemann-Weaver, arXiv:math/0312135 (Lemma 1 and the recalled excision facts); Blanchard-Dykema, arXiv:math/9911012 (Lemma 1.1 and Theorem 1.3, statements); Ueda, arXiv:math/0601706v4 (Section 1 and Proposition 2.2, Remark 2.3); Kishimoto-Ozawa-Sakai, arXiv:math/0110152 (Theorem 1.1 and the outline in Sections 2-4); Akemann-Wassermann-Weaver, arXiv:0705.1182 (Proposition 0.3); Calderon-Farah, arXiv:2006.06886v3 (abstract and the proposition in Section 7); Tanaka, arXiv:2609.26930 (abstract only). Every cited programme result was compared with its statement in the provider lesson on 15 Oct 2026. Checked by the program plan/checks_20261015/na_check.py (run b passes all 23 tests, output na_check_run_20261015b.txt; run a failed one test through a floating-point overflow in the check program, eigenvalues raised to the power 800, and was rerun after rescaling by the largest eigenvalue): r_h a r_h = h(a) r_h and tau(r_h) = 1/n for vector states of matrix algebras; the unitary e^{ia} of Lemma 2.2 of the first lesson in 20 random cases; the failure of cross-excision for equivalent states; the moment formula for norms under the normalized trace; a finite model of the expectation onto a peaking algebra (fixing, idempotence, bimodularity, trace preservation, positivity, the weights of the atoms); free products of group algebras of Z/3 and Z/2 (vanishing of centered alternating products, the formula of Exercise 5.2 of the third lesson, tau((uv)^n) = 0); the adjunction with trivial data as A * C[Z] (tau(v^n) = 0, tau(v a v* b) = tau(a) tau(b)); the matrix-unit identities of the adjunction model, the transfer relation (2.1) of the bridge lesson and the form of centered elements of M_2(D_1); the base algebra (tau(p_n) = 2^{-n}, f_0(a (x) b) = a_11 b_11); dependency closures on 50 random graphs; traces of matrix units under automorphisms.

open_obligations: Named hypothesis (KOS), the homogeneity theorem of Kishimoto, Ozawa and Sakai (Canad. Math. Bull. 46 (2003), Theorem 1.1; arXiv:math/0110152): used at every active step of the construction; not proved in the programme.

Missing foundation: (KOS) rests on Haagerup's invariant mean for the isometries of an injective von Neumann algebra (from his proof that nuclear C*-algebras are amenable), the separate normal extension of bounded bilinear forms, and the path arguments of Futamura, Kataoka and Kishimoto (arXiv:math/0104257); a foundation course on these would close it.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
